Samuel — thanks, copying legal and infra. Below is an initial exhibit we can put into the DPA; attaching a PDF and our subprocessor registry for review.

--- Proposed DPA Exhibit (Residency & Failover) ---
1) Residency Commitment: Redwood Inference will pin primary inference and associated ephemeral storage (KV-cache, request/response payloads) to the customer-designated region (EU) for all production traffic.

2) Transient Cross-Region Failover: In the event of an infrastructure incident (regional outage, catastrophic capacity shortfall) Redwood may perform temporary cross-region processing to preserve availability. Such processing is limited to a failure window no longer than 4 hours per incident by default, and will only be triggered when automated routing policies have exhausted local capacity and cross-region capacity is explicitly enabled for the customer.

3) Controls & Notification: Cross-region processing is subject to: (a) encryption-in-transit and at-rest; (b) KV-cache prefixes are scoped per-customer and cleared after failover; (c) KMS-managed keys for customer data are stored per-region when requested via the residency exhibit (see KMS paragraph). We will notify the customer within one hour of invoking cross-region failover and provide incident detail and duration.

4) KMS & Keys: Customers may elect to use region-bound KMS (customer-managed keys) via our KMS integration. If the customer elects region-bound KMS, Redwood will not export plaintext key material out of the region. If the customer uses Redwood-managed keys, key material is stored in the region where technically available; cross-region key wrapping events are logged and auditable.

5) Logs & Audit Trails: Application and inference telemetry (traces, token-level logs) for pinned requests will remain in-region. Aggregated operational metrics used for platform monitoring may be replicated for global observability but will be redacted of customer request bodies. Audit logs containing request identifiers and routing decisions will be retained for 90 days in-region; a copy may be stored in our central long-term retention system for legal/incident purposes but will be encrypted and access-restricted.

--- End exhibit ---

Attachments: redwood_dpa_residency_exhibit_v1.pdf, subprocessor_registry_20260630.csv

A couple of notes: the 4-hour default window is our standard emergency failover cap; we can reduce that for enterprise customers in dedicated contracts. For KMS we support both customer-managed keys (recommended for residency) and Redwood-managed keys.

If this looks good, Laura can convert it into a clean DPA exhibit and we can attach the SOC 2 link as requested.

Regards,
Jordan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Samuel — thanks for the clear asks. I converted Jordan's draft into binding exhibit language and tightened the failover cap so it's explicit. See the redlined exhibit text below; I will attach a PDF for signature after you confirm.

--- Final DPA Exhibit (Residency & Failover) ---
1) Residency Commitment: Redwood Inference shall process and store Customer Data originating from the European Economic Area (EEA) in data centers located within the EEA ("In-Region Processing") for the duration of the applicable Agreement. Secondary storage used for backups will likewise be geographically restricted to the EEA unless the Customer provides prior written consent.

2) Transient Cross-Region Failover: Notwithstanding Section 1, Redwood may temporarily route requests to non-EEA infrastructure only where a documented regional infrastructure outage prevents In-Region Processing and only after all configured regional capacity and routing options have been exhausted. Any cross-region processing invoked under this Section shall be limited to a cumulative maximum of four (4) hours per discrete outage event. Redwood will not extend cross-region processing beyond this four-hour cap without Customer's prior written consent. Redwood will provide notification to Customer within one (1) hour of invoking cross-region processing and provide a post-incident report detailing duration, scope, and mitigation steps.

3) KMS & Key Material: If Customer elects Customer-Managed Keys ("CMK") via supported KMS integrations, Customer will provision keys within an EEA region and grant Redwood a key-wrapping role. Redwood will not possess or export Customer plaintext key material. All key wrapping/unwrapping operations will be logged and made available to Customer for audit upon request.

4) Logs & Telemetry: Request payloads, debug-level logs, and KV-cache contents for in-region requests shall remain within the EEA. Aggregated platform metrics used for monitoring (e.g., token throughput, host-level CPU) may be replicated outside the EEA but will not contain request payloads or debug payloads. Audit logs containing routing decisions and non-sensitive identifiers shall be retained in-region for ninety (90) days. Redwood agrees to provide SOC 2 Type II report access under NDA and will supply a redacted subprocessor contact list highlighting subprocessors operating outside the EEA.

--- End Final Exhibit ---

Samuel — if this matches your requirements, confirm and we'll prepare the PDF exhibit for signature. Soojin — please provide the short CMK onboarding checklist (one pager) and the link to the SOC 2 package we can share under NDA.
